epic.intent:
Today, working in Dark Mechanicus means keeping GitHub Desktop or a terminal open beside it to see changes, commit, switch branches and push. This epic builds a simple GitHub Desktop clone into the app, so a person can do everyday Git work on any tracked folder without leaving it.

## What changes

- **Folder page with tabs.**
  - Clicking a folder opens its page with two tabs, **Source control** and **Epics**.
  - Source control opens first, and the app remembers the last tab used for each folder.
  - Source control works on any Git folder, including folders not set up for Dark Mechanicus. For those folders, the Epics tab shows the setup screen.
  - A folder that isn't a repository offers **Initialize repository**.
- **Changes.**
  - Every changed file is listed with its diff (unified, with line numbers).
  - Checkboxes choose which files to commit; sprint 3 adds choosing single lines and hunks.
  - A commit box takes a summary and a description.
  - **Discard changes** moves the discarded content to the OS trash first.
  - **Undo** reverts the last commit if it hasn't been pushed.
- **History.** The branch's commits, each with its message, changed files and diffs.
- **Branches.** A current-branch menu that can:
  - switch branches, either leaving uncommitted changes stashed on the old branch or bringing them along;
  - create, rename and delete branches (optionally deleting on the remote too);
  - merge a branch into the current one;
  - restore stashed changes.
- **Sync.** One Fetch / Pull / Push / Publish button with ahead/behind counts, progress and cancel, plus a background fetch.
- **Merge conflicts.** When a merge, pull or stash restore conflicts, the app shows:
  - the conflicted files with their conflict-marker counts;
  - Open in editor, Use mine / Use theirs, and Mark resolved for each file;
  - Abort merge and Commit merge.
- **GitHub sign-in.**
  - **Sign in to GitHub** sits in the sidebar footer. As in GitHub Desktop, the app shows a one-time code and opens github.com in the browser.
  - When signed in, git uses that account for HTTPS GitHub remotes.
  - When signed out, git falls back to the machine's own credentials (Git Credential Manager, keychain, SSH).
- **Clone.**
  - The sidebar **+** offers **Clone repository…**, from the signed-in account's repositories or from a URL, into a chosen folder.
  - Progress and cancel are shown, and the clone opens as a tracked folder.
- **Pull requests (GitHub repositories).**
  - The toolbar shows the current branch's pull request.
  - **Create pull request** opens GitHub's compare page, as GitHub Desktop does.
  - A list of open pull requests lets the person check one out, including pull requests from forks.

## Decisions (from the person, 2026-10-04)

- The folder page uses tabs, with Source control first and the last tab remembered per folder.
- Sign-in to GitHub uses the OAuth device flow, and the OS encrypts the token.
  - This needs a GitHub OAuth App with Device Flow enabled, which the person registers once.
  - Its client ID is public and is stored in the app.
- Beyond the baseline, this epic includes clone, pull requests, line-level commits and a merge conflict view.

## Design assumptions (planner; confirm at the sprint 1 checkpoint)

- **Where git runs.** Git runs in the Electron main process (`src/main/git`, `src/main/github`), reached through new `window.git` and `window.github` bridges.
  - It is not part of core's `CommandApi` or MCP. Agents keep using git directly.
  - Core's git adapter (`src/core/repo/git.ts`) stays read-only.
- **Which git.** The app uses the system `git` on PATH and does not bundle one. Without it, Source control says so and links to git-scm.com.
- **What counts as a change.** As in GitHub Desktop, the change set is the working tree compared with HEAD, and the index isn't shown. A commit resets the index to HEAD and then stages exactly what is checked.
- **Pull.** Pull merges (`--no-rebase`), never rebases.
- **Running repository programs.**
  - Opening a folder runs only git reads, with `core.fsmonitor`, external diff and textconv disabled. Looking at a repository never runs a program that the repository's config names.
  - Commits run the repository's hooks, as git does.
- **The GitHub token.**
  - It never reaches the renderer, logs, command lines or error text.
  - Git gets it through an environment-based credential helper scoped to `https://github.com`, and other helpers are cleared for that call.
- **Host.** Only GitHub.com is supported.

## Out of scope

- Git operations: rebase, force push, amend, cherry-pick, revert, tags, submodules and LFS.
- GitHub: creating GitHub repositories, GitHub Enterprise, GitHub Actions status, and editing pull requests in the app.
- Diff display: image diffs and a split diff view.

successCriteria.text: Clicking a tracked folder opens its page on the Source control tab. The last tab used is remembered per folder, and Source control works on Git folders that are not set up for Dark Mechanicus.

The Changes tab lists every changed file with its diff, and a commit with a summary and description contains exactly the checked files and selected lines. Discarded changes can be recovered from the OS trash, and the last unpushed commit can be undone.
The History tab lists the branch's commits, and each commit shows its message, changed files and diffs.

A person signs in to GitHub with a one-time code in the browser, sees the account in the app and can sign out. The token is stored only encrypted by the OS and never appears in the renderer, logs, command lines or error text.
Fetch, pull and push show ahead/behind counts and progress. They use the GitHub account for HTTPS GitHub remotes when signed in, and the machine's own Git credentials otherwise.

Branches can be created, switched (stashing or bringing changes), renamed, deleted and merged into the current branch. A conflicting merge, pull or stash restore can be resolved, aborted or committed from the app.
A repository can be cloned from the signed-in account's list or from a URL into a chosen folder, with progress and cancel, and then opens tracked in the sidebar.
For a GitHub repository, the current branch's pull request is shown, Create pull request opens GitHub's compare page, and open pull requests, including ones from forks, can be checked out.

bundle.rationale:
## Why three sprints

The sprints are ordered by risk and dependency, and each ends with something the person can use.

1. **Sprint 1: local work (DM-131 to DM-139, acceptance DM-130).** It needs no network and no credentials.
   - It lays the foundation every later ticket uses: the git runner, the readers, the `window.git` bridge and `DiffView`.
   - It already replaces most of GitHub Desktop's day-to-day use: see the changes, commit and browse history.
2. **Sprint 2: GitHub sign-in, sync, branches and conflicts (DM-141 to DM-148, acceptance DM-140).**
   - The credential work is the riskiest part, so it comes as early as its foundations allow.
   - Branches and conflicts come in the same sprint, because pulls and merges produce the conflicts.
3. **Sprint 3: the extras the person chose (DM-150 to DM-157, acceptance DM-149).** Clone, pull requests and line-level commits, plus the docs.

## The graph

**Sprint 1**
- The critical path is DM-131 (runner) → DM-132 (readers) → DM-133 (bridge) → DM-135 (folder tabs) → DM-137 (changes panel) → DM-139 (Fireguard).
- DM-134 (`DiffView`) runs beside DM-133, and DM-136 (commit operations) runs beside DM-135.
- DM-137 joins DM-135 and DM-136, and DM-138 (history) needs DM-135.

**Sprint 2**
- DM-141 (sign-in) unblocks DM-142 (account UI) and DM-143 (sync operations).
- DM-144 (sync button) joins DM-142 and DM-143.
- DM-145 (branch operations) needs DM-143, because deleting a remote branch pushes with the same credentials. DM-146 (branch menu) and DM-147 (conflicts) both build on DM-145.

**Sprint 3**
- There are three independent pairs: clone (DM-150 → DM-151), pull requests (DM-152 → DM-153) and line commits (DM-154 → DM-155).
- The docs ticket (DM-156) joins all three, so it documents what landed.

**Every sprint**
- Each sprint has its own Fireguard ticket, as delivery-standards requires: DM-139, DM-148 and DM-157. Each requires all of its sprint's work.
- The acceptance nodes check each ticket end to end on scratch repositories, in a built app with an isolated profile. They never touch the person's own folders or settings.

## Assumptions (planner, 2026-10-04)

- **Where git runs.**
  - Git runs in the main process (`src/main/git`, `src/main/github`), behind the new `window.git` and `window.github` bridges, outside core's `CommandApi` and MCP.
  - Agents keep using git directly, and core's git adapter stays read-only.
  - The precedent for main-only features is `boardRemovalFiles.ts`, `mcpJsonFile.ts` and `skillInstall.ts`.
- **Which git.** The system `git` on PATH is used; the app bundles none.
- **The change model is GitHub Desktop's.**
  - The change set is the working tree compared with HEAD, and the index is not shown.
  - A commit resets the index and stages exactly what is checked.
  - Pull merges (`--no-rebase`).
  - Discard moves content to the trash.
- **Running repository programs.**
  - Automatic reads disable `core.fsmonitor`, external diff and textconv, so a repository's config can't run programs just because it is viewed.
  - Commits run hooks as git does. This keeps `docs/product-plan.md`'s rule that tracking a folder never executes its code.
- **The GitHub token.**
  - The OAuth device flow stores the token encrypted with `safeStorage`, in `userData`.
  - Git receives the token through an environment-based credential helper scoped to `https://github.com`, with every other helper cleared for that call.
  - The Agents epic's rule that the app stores no vendor credentials covers agent CLIs, not this GitHub account, which the person asked for.
- **What acceptance can't do.** Completing a GitHub sign-in needs the person in their own browser. The acceptance nodes verify everything up to the real device code, and list the signed-in checks in the sprint report for the person to try at the checkpoint.

## Before sprint 2

The person registers a GitHub OAuth App with Device Flow enabled and gives its client ID, which is recorded in an epic comment (sprint 2's entry criterion). DM-141 puts that ID in `src/main/github/config.ts`.

## Overlap with other backlog epics

These epics touch the same renderer files: `chooseView.ts`, `selection.ts`, `App.tsx` and the sidebar.
- DM-135 replaces the `home` and `onboarding` main views with a tabbed `folder` view.
- The Conditionals epic (DM-111 adds a `conditional` selection) and the Agents epic (an Agents block per folder) were planned against the old views.

Whichever of those epics runs after this one must adapt to the folder page.

This is the planned final round for sprint 1, run once on the combined work.

1. **Combine** every accepted sprint 1 ticket on the sprint integration branch.
2. **Build** the app (`npm run build`) and run it with an isolated profile (a temporary `--user-data-dir`), so the person's tracked folders and settings are untouched.
3. **Prepare scratch repositories** in a temp folder; never use this repository's real state.
   - `scratch-a` has 250 commits, a merge commit, a renamed file, a binary file, a CRLF file, a file without a final newline, and a 5,000-line change.
   - `scratch-a` also sets `core.fsmonitor`, `diff.external` and a `textconv` driver to scripts that write marker files.
   - A local bare repository is `scratch-a`'s `origin`, for the unpushed checks.
   - `scratch-plain` is a folder that isn't a repository.
4. **Verify each item** below in the built app, with screenshots.
5. **Run the Definition of Done** on the combined branch.
   - Take Fireguard's grade from the sprint 1 Fireguard ticket, which must be accepted first.
   - Re-run Fireguard only if test files changed after that ticket.
6. **Squash** the sprint into one commit on `source-control`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `createGitRunner().run` spawns git with an argument array and no shell. It strips an inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, disables fsmonitor, and adds `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` for reads. A test shows each.
Writes and network operations for one repository run one at a time in request order, and reads are not held behind them. A test with a fake spawn shows the order.
A timeout or abort kills the git process tree and rejects with `timeout` or `cancelled`. A missing git binary rejects with `git_not_found`, and output over the limit rejects with `output_too_large`.
`classifyGitFailure` maps each listed failure to its code, with the stderr tail in `detail`, and anything unknown becomes `git_failed`. A test covers each row.
`pathArgs` and `refArg` refuse NUL, a leading `-`, absolute paths and `..` escapes, and `checkBranchName` reports git's verdict. A test covers each.
The tests were written first, and the touched tests, lint and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**. This is the first ticket of the Source control epic. Every later git operation goes through this runner, and nothing is visible to the person yet.

**Context**
- The only git code today is `src/core/repo/git.ts`. It is a read-only adapter for core: `execFile` with a 10 s timeout, `gitEnv()` at lines 110-116 and `safeArg()` at lines 136-141. Leave it unchanged.
- Source control is different. The person starts it, it writes (commit, push, merge), it streams progress, and it can run for minutes.
- It lives in a new `src/main/git/` folder in the main process, outside core's `CommandApi` and MCP. The precedent is `src/main/desktop/boardRemovalFiles.ts`.

**Build `src/main/git/runner.ts`**
- `createGitRunner(options?: { spawn?: SpawnFn; gitPath?: string; platform?: NodeJS.Platform }): GitRunner`, with `run(request: GitRunRequest): Promise<GitRunResult>`.
- `GitRunRequest = { cwd: string; args: readonly string[]; kind: 'read' | 'write' | 'network'; stdin?: string; env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; timeoutMs?: number; maxOutputBytes?: number; signal?: AbortSignal; onProgress?(line: string): void; acceptExitCodes?: readonly number[] }`.
- `GitRunResult = { code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string }`.
- Spawning: run `git` (or `gitPath`) with `child_process.spawn`, an argument array, no shell and `windowsHide: true`. Always prepend `-c core.quotepath=false -c color.ui=never -c core.fsmonitor=false`.
- Environment:
  - Start from `process.env` and remove `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` and `GIT_NAMESPACE`. This mirrors and extends core's `gitEnv()`.
  - Set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.
  - Force English messages so error classification stays stable (for example `LC_ALL=C` and `LANGUAGE=en`), and prove non-ASCII paths still round-trip.
  - `kind: 'read'` adds `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.
  - Merge `request.env` last. A later ticket passes credentials there, so it is never logged.
- Output:
  - Decode stdout and stderr as UTF-8.
  - Stop at `maxOutputBytes` (default 64 MiB) and reject with `output_too_large`.
  - `onProgress` receives stderr split on both `\r` and `\n`, because git redraws progress with `\r`.
- Timeouts: the default is 30 s for `read`, 120 s for `write` and none for `network`, which can only be cancelled.
- On timeout or abort:
  - kill the process tree: on Windows `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F`; elsewhere `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after 2 s;
  - reject with `timeout` or `cancelled`.
- Queue: `write` and `network` requests for the same repository (canonical `cwd`) run one at a time, in request order. Reads are never queued.
- Failures:
  - a non-zero exit code that isn't in `acceptExitCodes` rejects with a classified `GitError`;
  - a spawn `ENOENT` rejects with `git_not_found`.

**Build `src/shared/git/errors.ts` and `src/main/git/errors.ts`**
- Shared: a renderer-safe `GitErrorCode` union. Start with `git_not_found`, `not_repository`, `auth_required`, `auth_failed`, `rejected_non_fast_forward`, `merge_conflicts`, `local_changes_would_be_overwritten`, `nothing_to_commit`, `branch_exists`, `branch_not_fully_merged`, `remote_not_found`, `network_unreachable`, `index_locked`, `operation_in_progress`, `timeout`, `cancelled`, `output_too_large` and `git_failed`. Later tickets may add codes.
- Main:
  - `class GitError extends Error { code: GitErrorCode; detail: string }`;
  - `classifyGitFailure(result: GitRunResult, args: readonly string[]): GitError`. `detail` is the last 2,000 characters of stderr.
- Keep the stderr patterns in one table. Each row gets a test using output captured from real git in a temp repository, wherever it can be produced offline.

**Build `src/main/git/args.ts`**
- `pathArgs(paths)` returns `['--', ...paths]`. It refuses NUL, absolute paths, `..` segments that leave the repository, and empty strings.
- `refArg(name)` refuses a leading `-`, NUL and whitespace.
- `checkBranchName(runner, cwd, name)` runs `git check-ref-format --branch <name>` and returns `{ valid: boolean; normalized: string | null }`.

**Out of scope**: IPC, UI and any git operation beyond what the tests need.

**Verify** (write the tests first)
- `src/main/git/runner.test.ts` uses real temp repositories (`src/test/gitRepo.ts`), and a fake `spawn` where timing matters. It covers:
  - an inherited `GIT_DIR` does not leak;
  - reads get `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`;
  - progress is split on `\r`;
  - two writes to one repository run in order, and a read is not held behind them;
  - timeout and abort kill the child (the fake records the kill);
  - a bogus `gitPath` gives `git_not_found`;
  - a non-ASCII file name round-trips;
  - too much output gives `output_too_large`.
- `errors.test.ts` and `args.test.ts` cover each row and each refusal.
- Run the touched tests, lint and typecheck. The full gate runs at the checkpoint.

reasoning.rationale: Process spawning, per-repository queuing, Windows process-tree kills and error classification need careful tests first.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**. This ticket opens the bridge that every later Source control ticket extends. It requires the state and diff readers.

**Contract** (`src/shared/git/api.ts`)
```ts
export type GitResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: { code: GitErrorCode | 'invalid_input' | 'unauthorized'; message: string; detail?: string } }
export interface GitProgressEvent { folder: string; operationId: string; operation: string; phase: string; percent: number | null }
export interface GitApi {
  getState(folder: string): Promise<GitResult<RepoState>>
  getWorkingDiff(folder: string, request: { path: string; oldPath: string | null; kind: FileChangeKind; force?: boolean }): Promise<GitResult<FileDiff>>
  initRepository(folder: string): Promise<GitResult<RepoState>>
  onProgress(listener: (event: GitProgressEvent) => void): () => void
}
```

**Main** (`src/main/git/handlers.ts`, `src/main/git/ipc.ts`)
- `createGitHandlers(deps: { registry: Pick<FolderRegistry, 'resolve'>; runner: GitRunner; onUnexpectedError(error: unknown): void })`.
- Input checks:
  - each handler takes `unknown` arguments and validates them with zod, following `parseInput` in `src/main/desktop/handlers.ts:36-45`;
  - the folder must be tracked, resolved through the registry like `requireTracked` (`handlers.ts:90-97`); otherwise return `unauthorized`;
  - paths must be repository-relative and pass `pathArgs` (`src/main/git/args.ts`), so the renderer can't point git at other files.
- Errors:
  - a `GitError` becomes `{ ok: false }` with its code;
  - an unexpected error is logged through `onUnexpectedError` and returned as `git_failed`, without a stack;
  - nothing throws across IPC.
- `initRepository` runs `git init` in the tracked folder, refuses a folder that is already inside a repository, and returns the new state.
- `registerGitIpc(ipc: Pick<IpcMain, 'handle'>, handlers)` registers `git:getState`, `git:getWorkingDiff` and `git:initRepository`.
- `createProgressBroadcaster(send)` sends `GitProgressEvent`s to every window on `git:progress` (`webContents.send`). Later operations call it.
- Wiring:
  - wire all of this into `startDesktopBridge` in `src/main/desktop/bootstrap.ts`, with the same folder registry;
  - don't import `ipcMain` anywhere new: `src/main/ipcGuard.test.ts:254-265` must stay green.

**Preload and renderer**
- `src/preload/index.ts`: call `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('git', git)`.
  - Each method is one `ipcRenderer.invoke('git:<name>', …)`.
  - `onProgress` follows `autoUpdate.onEvent` (lines 9-15).
  - Add the typing to `src/renderer/src/window.d.ts`.
- `src/renderer/src/api/git.ts`: `callGit(promise)` unwraps a `GitResult` and throws `GitCommandError { code, message, detail }`. Follow `src/renderer/src/api/dm.ts:19-29`.
- `src/renderer/src/__mocks__/fakeGit.ts`: `FakeGit implements GitApi`. You can set its state and diffs per folder, and it lists the calls it received. Later UI tests assert on its state, not on `vi.fn`.

**Out of scope**: UI. Later tickets add their own channels, preload methods and `FakeGit` methods in the same pattern.

**Verify** (write the tests first)
- `src/main/git/handlers.test.ts` uses a fake registry and real temp repositories. It covers:
  - a tracked folder and an untracked folder;
  - malformed input and a path with `..`;
  - `initRepository` on a plain folder and inside a repository;
  - error mapping.
- `src/main/git/ipc.test.ts` uses the fake ipc from `src/main/desktop/ipc.test.ts` and checks that the channel names reach the handlers.
- A broadcaster test checks that events reach listeners until they unsubscribe.
- Run `npm run dev`, track this repository, and call `await window.git.getState('<path>')` in devtools. Put the output in the evidence.
- Run the touched tests, lint and typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: A new IPC surface across shared contracts, main handlers, the preload and the renderer, with input validation and folder authorization.

Size: **medium**. These are the main-process operations behind the Changes panel. This ticket requires the bridge.

**API** (extend `GitApi` in `src/shared/git/api.ts`, the handlers, `src/main/git/ipc.ts`, the preload and `FakeGit`)
- `commit(folder, { summary: string; description: string; files: Array<{ path: string; oldPath: string | null }> }): Promise<GitResult<{ oid: string }>>`
- `undoLastCommit(folder): Promise<GitResult<{ summary: string; description: string }>>`
- `discardChanges(folder, { files: FileChange[] }): Promise<GitResult<RepoState>>`

Every path goes through `pathArgs` and must appear in the current status.

**Commit** (`src/main/git/commit.ts`)
1. Refuse an empty summary or an empty file list with `invalid_input`. Refuse while `inProgress` is set, with `operation_in_progress`; sprint 2's conflict ticket adds merge commits.
2. Reset the index to HEAD (`git reset -q --`; on an unborn branch, `git read-tree --empty`), so only the chosen files are committed, matching what the panel shows.
3. Stage the chosen files with `git add -A -- <paths>`. A rename passes both its old and new path.
4. Run `git commit -F -` with the message on stdin: the summary, then a blank line and the description when there is one, both trimmed. Hooks run as git runs them; a failing hook returns `git_failed` with the hook output in `detail`.
5. Return the new HEAD oid. Files that weren't chosen stay changed and unstaged, as intended.

**Undo last commit**
- Undo is allowed only when HEAD exists, isn't a merge commit, and isn't on any remote branch (`git branch -r --contains HEAD` is empty). Otherwise return `invalid_input` with the reason: "already pushed", "merge commit" or "no commits".
- Read the message (`git log -1 --format=%B`), then run `git reset --soft HEAD~1`. For the root commit, run `git update-ref -d HEAD`.
- Return the summary (the first paragraph) and the description (the rest).

**Discard** (`src/main/git/discard.ts`)
- Inject `trashItem(path): Promise<void>`. In `bootstrap.ts` it is Electron's `shell.trashItem`.
- What happens to each kind of change:
  - modified or typechange: copy the working file into a new temp folder under its own name, move that copy to the trash, then run `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`;
  - deleted: run `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` (there is nothing to save);
  - untracked: move the file to the trash;
  - added to the index but not in HEAD: run `git rm -q --cached -- <path>`, then move the file to the trash;
  - renamed: move the new file to the trash, as for an added file, and restore the old path from HEAD.
- Return the new state.

**Verify** (write the tests first, on real temp repositories)
- Commit:
  - only the chosen files are committed, even when another file was staged earlier;
  - a rename;
  - the first commit of an unborn repository;
  - summary-only and summary-plus-description messages;
  - a failing `pre-commit` hook.
- Undo restores the changes and returns the message. It is refused after a push to a local bare remote, for a merge commit and when there are no commits.
- Discard each kind with a fake trash that records what it received, and check the trashed content.
- Untracked folders and paths outside the repository are refused.
- Run the touched tests, lint and typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Writes to the repository: index reset and staging, undo safety rules and recoverable discards need careful tests first.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**. Sign-in to GitHub through the OAuth device flow, as GitHub Desktop offers. Nothing in the renderer ever sees the token.

**Before starting**: the GitHub OAuth App's client ID is in a comment on this epic (the sprint 2 entry criterion). It is public, because the device flow needs no client secret.

**Config** (`src/main/github/config.ts`)
- `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` is the client ID from the epic comment.
- `GITHUB_SCOPES = 'repo read:user workflow'`. `workflow` lets a push change `.github/workflows`, which GitHub Desktop also requests.

**Device flow** (`src/main/github/deviceFlow.ts`; inject `fetch`, `sleep` and `now`)
- `startDeviceFlow()` sends a POST to `https://github.com/login/device/code` (`Accept: application/json`, form body `client_id` and `scope`). It returns `{ deviceCode, userCode, verificationUri, expiresAt, intervalSeconds }`.
- `pollForToken(deviceCode, intervalSeconds, signal)` sends a POST to `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`, and handles each answer:
  - `authorization_pending`: wait the interval and poll again;
  - `slow_down`: add 5 s to the interval;
  - `expired_token` or `access_denied`: end with `sign_in_expired` or `sign_in_denied`;
  - `incorrect_client_credentials`, `device_flow_disabled` or `unsupported_grant_type`: end with `sign_in_misconfigured` (the OAuth App needs Device Flow enabled);
  - an abort ends with `cancelled`, and a network failure with `network_unreachable`.

**API client** (`src/main/github/client.ts`)
- `createGithubClient({ fetch, getToken, appVersion })` provides `getUser()`, which calls `GET https://api.github.com/user` with these headers:
  - `Authorization: Bearer <token>`;
  - `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`;
  - `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`;
  - `User-Agent: DarkMechanicus/<version>`.
- Later tickets add calls to this client.
- A 401 returns `auth_required` and signs the account out locally, because the token was revoked.
- Keep the `X-OAuth-Scopes` header value with the account.

**Account store** (`src/main/github/accountStore.ts`)
- Inject `{ isAvailable, encrypt, decrypt }`. In bootstrap these are Electron's `safeStorage`.
- The file is `userData/github-account.json`: `{ version: 1, login, name, scopes, token }`, where `token` is the base64 of `safeStorage.encryptString(token)`.
- Write it atomically (a tmp file, then rename), like `src/main/desktop/folderRegistry.ts:107-120`.
- Refuse to sign in when `isEncryptionAvailable()` is false, with `secure_storage_unavailable`. Never fall back to plain text.
- `getToken()` is main-only, and `signOut()` deletes the file.

**Bridge**
- Files: `src/shared/github/api.ts`, `src/main/github/handlers.ts`, `src/main/github/ipc.ts`, the preload's `window.github`, `src/renderer/src/api/github.ts` and `src/renderer/src/__mocks__/fakeGithub.ts`.
```ts
export interface GithubAccountView { login: string; name: string | null }
export interface GithubApi {
  getAccount(): Promise<GitResult<GithubAccountView | null>>
  startSignIn(): Promise<GitResult<{ userCode: string; verificationUri: string; expiresAt: string }>>
  cancelSignIn(): Promise<GitResult<null>>
  signOut(): Promise<GitResult<null>>
  onAccountChanged(listener: (account: GithubAccountView | null) => void): () => void
  onSignInFailed(listener: (error: { code: string; message: string }) => void): () => void
}
```
- `startSignIn`:
  - starts the flow, opens `verificationUri` in the browser (`shell.openExternal`), returns the code, and polls in the background;
  - starting again cancels the previous attempt;
  - success stores the account and broadcasts `github:accountChanged`, and failure broadcasts `github:signInFailed`.
- Register the handlers through the guarded registrar in `bootstrap.ts`, like the git bridge.
- Export a main-side `githubSession` (`getAccount`, `getToken`) for the later sync, clone and pull request tickets.

**Token rules**: the token never crosses IPC and never appears in a log line, an error message or `detail`. It is decrypted only in main, only when needed.

**Verify** (write the tests first)
- The device flow, with a fake fetch and clock: pending then slow_down then success; expired; denied; misconfigured; cancel.
- The store: a round trip with fake crypto, refusal when encryption is unavailable, sign-out deleting the file, and the file never holding the plain token.
- Handlers and broadcasts: search every result and event payload for the fake token string and assert it is absent. A 401 signs the account out.
- Run the touched tests, lint and typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Handles a long-lived credential: a mistake in storage, IPC or logging leaks the person's GitHub token and is hard to spot.

For an HTTPS github.com remote while signed in, git gets the account's login and token from an environment-based credential helper scoped to https://github.com, and every other configured helper is cleared. An offline `git credential fill` test proves both, and the token appears in no argument, log or error detail.

A non-fast-forward push, an auth failure, a conflicting pull and a network failure each return their own code. Cancel stops a running operation with `cancelled`.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**. Fetch, pull, push and publish, using the GitHub account's credentials when signed in. This ticket requires the sign-in ticket (`githubSession`).

**Remotes** (`src/main/git/remotes.ts`)
- `listRemotes(runner, root)` returns `[{ name, fetchUrl, pushUrl }]` from `git remote -v`.
- A pure `parseGithubRemote(url)` returns `{ owner, repo } | null`:
  - it accepts `https://github.com/o/r(.git)`, `git@github.com:o/r(.git)` and `ssh://git@github.com/o/r(.git)`;
  - anything else is null;
  - sprint 3 uses it for pull requests.
- The sync remote is the upstream's remote, else `origin`. With neither, return `remote_not_found`.

**Credentials** (`src/main/git/credentials.ts`)
- `credentialArgs(remoteUrl, session)` returns extra args and env when the URL is `https://github.com/…` and an account is signed in:
  - args: first `-c credential.helper=`, which clears every configured helper, Git Credential Manager included; then `-c credential.https://github.com.helper=!f() { echo username="$DM_GITHUB_LOGIN"; echo password="$DM_GITHUB_TOKEN"; }; f`;
  - env: `DM_GITHUB_LOGIN` and `DM_GITHUB_TOKEN`, passed through `request.env` and never logged.
- Otherwise (signed out, SSH or other hosts) it returns nothing, and git uses the machine's own credentials (GCM, keychain, SSH agent). `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` stays, so nothing waits on a terminal.
- The token never appears in an argument. As a second guard, scrub the token string from any stderr before it becomes a `detail`.

**Progress** (`src/main/git/progress.ts`)
- A pure `parseProgressLine(line)` returns `{ phase, percent }` for git's lines: `Counting objects`, `Compressing objects`, `Receiving objects:  45% (450/1000)`, `Resolving deltas`, `Writing objects` and `remote: …`.
- Feed it from the runner's `onProgress`, and send `GitProgressEvent`s through the broadcaster.

**Operations** (`src/main/git/sync.ts`; extend `GitApi` and the rest of the bridge)
- Each operation takes `{ operationId: string }` from the renderer, so the renderer can cancel it. All use `kind: 'network'`.
- `fetch(folder, { operationId })` runs `git fetch --prune --progress <remote>`.
- `pull(folder, { operationId })` runs `git pull --no-rebase --no-edit --progress <remote> <branch>`: it merges, never rebases. Conflicts return `merge_conflicts`, and the state then shows `inProgress: 'merge'`.
- `push(folder, { operationId })`:

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**. The main-process branch and stash operations. This ticket requires the sync operations, because deleting a remote branch pushes with the same credentials.

**Types** (`src/shared/git/branches.ts`)
```ts
export interface BranchInfo { name: string; kind: 'local' | 'remote'; remote: string | null; upstream: string | null; ahead: number; behind: number; lastCommitAt: string; isCurrent: boolean }
export interface BranchList { current: string | null; defaultBranch: string | null; branches: BranchInfo[] }
export interface StashInfo { ref: string /* stash@{n} */; branch: string; createdAt: string; files: CommitFile[] }
```

**Operations** (`src/main/git/branches.ts`, `src/main/git/stash.ts`; extend `GitApi` and the rest of the bridge)
- Every name goes through `refArg` and `checkBranchName`.
- `listBranches(folder)`:
  - runs `git for-each-ref --format=… refs/heads refs/remotes`, skipping `*/HEAD`;
  - takes `defaultBranch` from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, else `main` or `master` when it exists.
- `checkBranchName(folder, name)` returns `{ valid, normalized }`, for live validation.
- `createBranch(folder, { name, startPoint: 'current' | 'default' })` runs `git switch -c <name> [<default>]`. Uncommitted changes come along, and an existing name returns `branch_exists`.
- `switchBranch(folder, { name, uncommitted: 'stash' | 'bring' })`:
  - a remote-only branch is checked out as a local tracking branch (`git switch --track <remote>/<name>`);
  - `stash` runs `git stash push --include-untracked -m "dm-stash:<current branch>"`, then switches;
  - `bring` runs `git switch <name>`. If git refuses, return `local_changes_would_be_overwritten` and change nothing;
  - switching never pops a stash by itself.
- `renameBranch(folder, { from, to })` runs `git branch -m`.
- `deleteBranch(folder, { name, deleteRemote: boolean, force: boolean })`:
  - refuses the current branch;
  - runs `git branch -d` (`-D` with `force`); an unmerged branch without `force` returns `branch_not_fully_merged`;
  - with `deleteRemote`, then runs `git push <remote> --delete <name>` as a network operation with the sync credentials.
- `mergeIntoCurrent(folder, { branch })` runs `git merge --no-edit <branch>`. Conflicts return `merge_conflicts`.
- Stashes:
  - `listStashes(folder)` returns only the `dm-stash:` stashes for the current branch, with their files (`git stash show --name-status -z --include-untracked <ref>`);
  - `restoreStash(folder, ref)` runs `git stash pop <ref>`. Conflicts return `merge_conflicts`, and git keeps the stash;
  - `discardStash(folder, ref)` runs `git stash drop <ref>`.

**Verify** (write the tests first, on real temp repositories with a local bare remote)
- Listing: local, remote, current and default branches, and ahead/behind.
- Create from the current branch and from the default branch.
- Switch with stash and with bring, including a refusal that changes nothing, and switch to a remote-only branch.
- Rename.
- Delete: merged, not merged, forced, and with the remote branch.
- Merge: clean and conflicting.
- Stashes: list, restore (clean and conflicting) and discard.
- Run the touched tests, lint and typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Branch and stash operations with safety rules (no data loss on refused switches, remote deletion) across many git edge cases.

Size: **medium**. The merge conflict view, from the main-process operations to the UI. This ticket requires the branch operations: merges and stash restores create conflicts, and so do pulls.

**Main** (`src/main/git/conflicts.ts`; extend `GitApi` and the rest of the bridge)
- `getConflicts(folder)` returns `{ ourBranch: string | null; theirLabel: string | null /* from MERGE_MSG's first line */; files: Array<{ path: string; kind: 'both_modified' | 'both_added' | 'deleted_by_us' | 'deleted_by_them' | 'both_deleted' | 'added_by_us' | 'added_by_them'; markers: number }> }`. `markers` counts the lines starting with `<<<<<<< ` in the working file, and is 0 when the file is missing.
- `resolveWith(folder, { path, side: 'ours' | 'theirs' })` runs `git checkout --ours|--theirs -- <path>`, then `git add -- <path>`. When the chosen side deleted the file, it runs `git rm -- <path>` instead.
- `markResolved(folder, { path })` runs `git add -- <path>`. While `markers > 0`, it is refused with `conflict_markers_remain`.
- `abortMerge(folder)` runs `git merge --abort`.
- `commitMerge(folder, { summary?: string; description?: string })` is refused with `merge_conflicts` while unresolved files remain. Otherwise it runs `git commit --no-edit`, or `-F -` with the given message.
- `abortOperation(folder)`, for a rebase, cherry-pick or revert started outside the app, runs `git rebase|cherry-pick|revert --abort`.
- `openInEditor(folder, path)` calls `shell.openPath(<absolute path>)`, which is injected. The path must be in the repository.

**UI** (`src/renderer/src/source/ConflictsPanel.tsx`)
- When `inProgress === 'merge'`, a banner sits above the Changes list: "Merging <their label> into <our branch>: N conflicted files". It has **Abort merge** (which asks for confirmation) and **Commit merge** (enabled once nothing is unresolved).
- Conflicted files are listed first. Each shows "N conflicts" or "Resolved", with:
  - **Open in editor**;
  - **Use mine (<our branch>)** and **Use theirs (<their label>)**;
  - **Mark resolved**, disabled while markers remain. The count refreshes with the state.
- While merging, Commit merge replaces the commit box, and the diff pane shows the working file's diff with the markers.
- For a rebase, cherry-pick or revert in progress, a banner says "A <operation> is in progress. Finish it in a terminal, or abort it here.", with **Abort**.
- A pull, merge or stash restore that returns `merge_conflicts` lands here after the refresh.

**Verify** (write the tests first)
- Main tests, on real temp repositories:
  - a conflicting merge with both_modified, deleted_by_them and added files;
  - marker counts;
  - ours and theirs;
  - Mark resolved refused while markers remain;
  - abort;
  - commit merge refused, then allowed;
  - aborting a rebase started from the command line.
- UI tests with `FakeGit`: the banner, the file actions, Commit merge replacing the commit box, and the abort confirmation.

- `name` must:
  - contain no path separators, and not be `.` or `..`;

Size: **medium**. Main-process pull request data and checkout for GitHub repositories. Sprint 2's `parseGithubRemote`, `githubSession`, credentials and branch switching are in place.

**Types** (`src/shared/github/pullRequests.ts`)
```ts
export interface PullRequestSummary { number: number; title: string; author: string; isDraft: boolean; url: string; updatedAt: string; baseRef: string; headRef: string; headRepoFullName: string | null /* null when the fork was deleted */; fromFork: boolean }
export interface PullRequestInfo { repository: { owner: string; repo: string } | null; current: PullRequestSummary | null; open: PullRequestSummary[] }
```

**Operations** (`src/main/github/pullRequests.ts`; they take a folder, so extend `GitApi`)
- The GitHub repository is the upstream's remote, else `origin`, parsed with `parseGithubRemote`. A non-GitHub repository returns `{ repository: null, current: null, open: [] }`.
- `getPullRequests(folder)`:
  - signed out, returns `auth_required`;
  - calls `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open&per_page=100`, up to 3 pages;
  - `current` is the open pull request whose head is the current branch in this repository: `head.repo.full_name` equals `owner/repo`, and `head.ref` equals the branch name or the upstream's branch name;
  - results are cached for 60 s per folder unless a refresh is asked.
- `checkoutPullRequest(folder, { number, uncommitted: 'stash' | 'bring' })` reuses sprint 2's switch rules for uncommitted changes.
  - Same repository: fetch the head branch, and switch to a local branch tracking it (created when missing).
  - Fork: run `git fetch <remote> refs/pull/<n>/head`, then switch to `pr/<n>`, created at `FETCH_HEAD`. When `pr/<n>` exists, switch to it and run `git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD`; a non-fast-forward returns `rejected_non_fast_forward`.
  - `pr/<n>` has no upstream; pushing it back to the fork is out of scope.
- `getCompareUrl(folder)` returns `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/compare/<default branch>...<branch>?expand=1`, which is GitHub Desktop's Create pull request. It returns `needs_push` when the branch has no upstream or is ahead of it.
- `getCommitUrl(folder, oid)` returns `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/commit/<oid>`, for History's View on GitHub.

- With real temp repositories and a local bare remote, checkout:

  - a fork pull request, made by creating `refs/pull/1/head` in the bare repository.

tickets.body:
Size: **small**. This is sprint 3's only Fireguard run. Fireguard is slow (100× flake isolation and mutation), so no other ticket in the sprint runs it, and workers run only their targeted tests. The sprint 3 acceptance ticket takes Fireguard's grade from this ticket.

1. **Wait** until every other sprint 3 work ticket is accepted and combined on the sprint integration branch. That branch was made from `source-control` at the sprint's start.
2. **Grade** with `npm run fireguard -- --json` on that branch:
   - set `FIREGUARD_BASE_REF` to the sprint's start commit;
   - Fireguard grades only committed changes;
   - on Windows, set `FIREGUARD_TEST_COMMAND='node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run'`, because of the npx spawn quirk.
3. **Fix any F:** rewrite each test graded F and re-grade until nothing is F.
   - Don't change production code to raise a grade.
   - If a finding points at a real bug in production code, fail the attempt with the finding, so the orchestrator can send it back to the ticket that owns that code.
4. **Record** the letter grade, the score, the graded files and each finding in the evidence.

Out of scope: lint, typecheck, the full test suite, deadcode and build, because the acceptance ticket runs those once.

reasoning.rationale: Running fireguard is mechanical, but rewriting a test graded F takes judgement about what the test should assert.
